criteria.text: For every recorte in `test/aggregate.test.ts`'s existing `recortes` list, for every pair drawn from `persons`, once `buildGraphAggregates(persons)` has run for the window, the new compare fast query renders byte-identical `about_a`/`about_b`/`terms` to today's live `compareQuery` — at the production `TOP` (200), no fixture doc additions needed.

For every recorte in the same list, for every person, with both `a` and `b` restricted to `all` or `source:<one of SOURCES>`, the new lenses fast query renders byte-identical output to today's live `lensesQuery`, once the window is built.

A recorte outside `precomputable(q)` (a `domain`, a `lean`, a comma `source` list, `country=pt`, `country=all`, or a `days` outside `DAYS`) still runs `/api/compare` fully live, unchanged output from before this issue.
A `domain:` or `lean:` lens on either side of `/api/people/:id/lenses`, or a `days` outside `DAYS` on either side, keeps the whole lenses request live, unchanged output from before this issue.

With `buildGraphAggregates(persons, DAYS, top)` run at a shrunk `top` (mirroring `test/aggregate.test.ts`'s existing "ceiling on graph_terms" pattern), there exists at least one fixture pair, window and `limit` in `SMALL_LIMITS` where the compare fast path returns `null` on one side for a term the other person genuinely used (the new, documented meaning) — and, at every `limit` in `SMALL_LIMITS` under that same shrunk build, every key belonging to a side's own top-`limit`-by-count or top-`limit`-by-weighted-PMI selection still reads its exact figure on that side, never `null`.
A `source` with zero docs for one or both persons in scope (fixture's `senado`) still answers the compare/lenses fast path: `about` reads `0` on that side and `terms` is `[]`, not a fallback to live.
`tone` on both routes is `null` wherever no GDELT doc contributed on that side, identical between the fast and the live path.

`docsText` (`test/docs.ts`) states that a `null` side on `/api/compare`/`/api/people/:id/lenses` can mean the term was used below the precomputed aggregate's own kept threshold, not only zero documents.
`docsText` states, in plain pt-BR, that a word drawn fully to one end of the compare or lenses ruler can mean the other side used it too, just below what the precomputed build kept.
`/compare/bridges` and `/lenses/bridges`: every existing `test/graph.test.ts` assertion for them still passes unmodified — still two live statements, same output.
Every existing `risingQuery`/`risingFor` test in `test/graph.test.ts` still passes unmodified; no fast path exists for rising after this issue.

`pnpm bench`'s `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` of the new compare and lenses fast builders, run against production-shaped data on a fast-eligible recorte, reads under 200 ms warm and touches only `graph_terms`/`graph_scopes` (primary-key reads), no scan of `doc_terms`/`docs` — manual step, since the suite runs against the in-memory fixture, not production data.

`test/docs-drift.test.ts` is unrelated to this issue (it covers the collector registry against `docs/sources.md`) and needs no new criterion here.
